transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm just... having some trouble at work lately. I do bookkeeping, and... I guess I've been doing some things that don't make a lot of sense. Like, I'll start lining up all the receipts across the floor instead of filing them. Or I have to tap the calculator in sets of nine before I can use it. Sometimes I just... stand by the copier with my hands up in the air, and I don't really know why until someone comes over and asks if I'm alright. So, that's why I'm here.
When you do things like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator nine times, do you notice an anxious thought or uncomfortable feeling beforehand that the action seems to relieve?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I'm anxious. It's just... I just do it. I don't really feel anything beforehand.
Besides these movements, have you noticed yourself making any repeated sounds, noises, or words that you can't seem to control?
No. I don't think so. Just the... the things I mentioned.
Have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others find strange or hard to believe?

Um... I guess maybe a little. Sometimes, when I'm just sitting at my desk, or... or walking home, I'll hear this voice. It's a man's voice. He just says random things, like... "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It sounds real. I usually look around, but... there's no one there.
How long have you been noticing these behaviors—like lining up receipts, tapping, and hearing that voice—has it been going on for weeks, or longer, like months?

Um... it's been longer than a few weeks. I guess... maybe about ten months? It just kind of started building up back when I began taking some evening accounting courses... while still working my bookkeeping job. So, yeah... around then.
Do you ever feel that people at work or elsewhere are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you in some way?

Um... not really people, no. It's more... well, the numbers. I know it sounds strange, but... sometimes I look at the invoice totals or account numbers, and... it feels like they mean something else. Like they're messages. About me. Even when my supervisor looks at them and says they're just normal entries, I still... I don't know, I still feel like they're tracking me, waiting to see if I figure out the pattern.

When you find yourself standing still with your hands raised like that, do you ever stay frozen in that position for a long time, become unable to speak, or resist when someone tries to move your arms or reposition you?

Um... no, I don't think I resist or anything. It's just... part of these things I've started doing at work and school that... that don't really make sense. I'll just be standing by the copier with my hands held up... and I guess I just stay like that until someone asks if I'm okay. Then I put them down. I don't really know why I do it.
Aside from standing with your hands up, have there been times when you become completely unresponsive or stop talking for a while, even when people are trying to get your attention?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I still talk to people. I don't just stop talking.

Would you say the hand-raising and freezing episodes happen almost every day and are the main problem, or do they occur only occasionally compared to how often you hear the voice or feel the numbers are sending you messages?

Um... the hands thing is just sometimes. The other stuff happens more. Like... the voice. I hear it a lot when I'm alone at my desk, or walking home. It's... it's a man's voice. He says things like, 'check line seven' or 'you missed the sign.' It's loud enough that I actually look around to see who's there, but... nobody is. So, yeah. That happens more often.

latest_inference.note: Duration now confirmed at ~10 months, meeting schizophrenia duration criteria. Prominent auditory hallucinations and bizarre referential/persecutory delusions (numbers as coded messages) dominate the picture and occur far more frequently than the odd motor behaviors. The hand-raising/freezing episodes lack true catatonic features (no mutism, negativism, waxy flexibility, or sustained unresponsiveness), so catatonic subtype is ruled out in favor of paranoid subtype.
